advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the `rebar.edit_ticket(..., parent=epic_local)` staging call so a `CommandError` from `_resolve_new_parent` (e.g. epic not in open/in_progress local status) reports as SETUP FAILED rather than an unattributed raw exception.
evidence: composer.py:460-461: `elif key == "parent": out["parent_id"] = _resolve_new_parent(value, resolved, tracker, reduce_ticket)`
composer.py:503-514: `status = ... ; if status not in ("open", "in_progress"): ... raise CommandError(...)` — the fail-closed parent-status gate

Docstring lines 1215-1218 claim the cell exists to prevent 'an unattributable failure of exactly the kind the SETUP-vs-defect split in this module exists to prevent', yet an edit_ticket CommandError would be exactly such an unattributed raw exception.
Sibling cell at line 1571/1597 sets the parent via `dc_transport.set_parent` + inbound priming, bypassing `_resolve_new_parent` entirely.
advisory.finding: The cell attaches the parent via `rebar.edit_ticket(child_local, parent=epic_local)`, which runs the local `_resolve_new_parent` fail-closed cascade (parent must be open/in_progress, must exist, not-self, no cycle). The call is unwrapped, so a `CommandError` from that gate — e.g. if the seeded epic imported with a non-open local status — surfaces as a raw unattributed test error rather than the 'SETUP FAILED' attribution the cell's own docstring promises. Sibling cells avoid this by establishing the parent through inbound import, which never touches this gate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture and assert HTTP 200 on the pre-pass `before` read of the Epic Link, mirroring the status check the sibling transport cell performs, so a failed read cannot masquerade as 'no prior Epic Link'.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py:1256: `assert not before_link, (` — precondition passes when before_link is None
Sibling transport cell asserts status explicitly — line 1171: `assert status == 200 and isinstance(body, dict), (` before trusting the read-back.
advisory.finding: The pre-pass 'before' read does not assert HTTP 200, unlike the sibling transport-level cell. `before = dc_request(...)[1] or {}` silently coerces a failed/non-dict read to `{}`, so the 'child carries no prior Epic Link' precondition (line 1256) can pass vacuously when the read actually failed.
